title: 2011 HMMT February Guts Problem 2
statement: Let \(a \star b=\sin a \cos b\) for all real numbers \(a\) and \(b\). If \(x\) and \(y\) are real numbers such that \(x \star y-y \star x=1\), what is the maximum value of \(x \star y+y \star x\) ?

solutions.text:
1
We have \(x \star y+y \star x=\sin x \cos y+\cos x \sin y=\sin (x+y) \leq 1\). Equality is achieved when \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}\) and \(y=0\). Indeed, for these values of \(x\) and \(y\), we have \(x \star y-y \star x=\sin x \cos y-\cos x \sin y=\sin (x-y)=\) \(\sin \frac{\pi}{2}=1\).
